errors.evidence: The figure contains three separate pie charts, but the description refers to it as a single chart.
Each of the three pie charts in the figure has four slices, not five. The description incorrectly states there are five slices in a single chart.

errors.text_span: each representing a distinct category: “easy” colored green and approximately 55.4%, “medium” colored purple and around 58.8%, “hard” colored pink and approximately 37.3%
errors.evidence: The description incorrectly identifies the titles of the three charts ('easy', 'medium', 'hard') as categories or slices within a single chart. The colors are also wrong; for example, no slice is colored purple or pink.

The description invents a slice category called "Zero-Shot" with a value of 39.9%. In the figure, "Zero-Shot" is a label for the entire set of charts, not a category within a chart, and the value 39.9% does not appear anywhere.

The description incorrectly maps the value 18.1% to the category "N+K-". In the 'hard' chart, 18.1% corresponds to the "N+K+" category. The actual values for "N+K-" are 1.7%, 1.8%, and 6.7% across the three charts.
The description fails to mention the main categories displayed in the charts and explained in the legend: "N+K+", "N-K+", and "N-K-". It only mentions "N+K-" and assigns it an incorrect value.

errors.text_span: the slices appear ordered from largest to smallest in terms of their area
errors.evidence: While this observation is coincidentally correct for all three individual charts, applying it to the single, non-existent chart described by the model is misleading and stems from the fundamental misinterpretation of the figure's structure.
